extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of common objects in natural context, with instance-level segmentation masks and captions, designed for object detection, segmentation, and scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.citeAs: T. Lin, M. Maire, S. Belongie, J. Hays, P. Perona, D. Ramanan, P. Dollár, and C. L. Zitnick, "Microsoft COCO: Common objects in context," in ECCV, 2014.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were gathered using a pipeline that harvested candidate images containing contextual relationships and non-iconic object views. The authors used Amazon Mechanical Turk for category labeling, instance spotting, instance segmentation, segmentation verification, and crowd labeling. They also added five written caption descriptions to each image.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Web API, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Photos/images from Flickr and images retrieved via Google or Bing image search and scene-based queries; candidate images were also collected using object-object and object-scene query pairs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was released in two parts: the first half in 2014 and the second half planned for 2015.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Near-duplicate images were explicitly removed using a duplicate detection method, and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize near duplicates across splits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid or iconic images were filtered out from candidate image grids; images were organized into train, validation, and test splits; only the 2014 release included segmentation masks for a subset of 80 categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation proceeded in stages: category labeling using a hierarchical super-category approach, instance spotting for all instances of labeled categories, instance segmentation for each object instance, and segmentation verification. For category labeling and instance spotting, 8 workers annotated each image. For segmentation verification, 3 annotators initially reviewed each segmentation, with 2 additional workers added if needed; segmentations not receiving at least 4 of 5 favorable votes were discarded. The paper also states that five written captions were added to each image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper analyzed worker precision and recall for category labeling, comparing AMT workers with expert co-authors. Ground truth was computed using majority vote of experts for one analysis and leave-one-out evaluation for another. The union of 8 AMT workers achieved greater recall than any expert worker. For segmentation verification, borderline cases were accepted or rejected based on 4/5 favorable votes.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 workers per image for category labeling; 8 workers per image for instance spotting; 3 to 5 workers per segmented instance for verification; 5 written captions per image.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For category selection, several children ranging in ages from 4 to 8 were asked to name objects they saw in indoor and outdoor environments. The paper does not provide demographics for AMT annotators.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset was split for a faster release schedule, with the first half released in 2014 and the second half planned for 2015. The paper states that MS COCO will evolve and grow over time and that up-to-date information is available online.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes people as an object category and mentions person instances, but the paper does not state collection of sensitive human attributes such as gender, age, ethnicity, language, or socioeconomic status.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance object recognition, detection, segmentation, and scene understanding in natural environments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes a preference for non-iconic images and discusses dataset bias and contextual differences relative to prior datasets, but it does not explicitly characterize specific biases within MS COCO beyond these design choices.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The 2014 release includes segmentation masks for only 80 of the 91 categories. Some categories were omitted because they had too many instances, were ambiguous and difficult to label, or had too few instances. The paper also notes that crowd-labeled regions are ignored for evaluation and that the dataset is more difficult than PASCAL VOC.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Designed for training and evaluation of object detection and segmentation algorithms, including bounding-box detection, instance segmentation, and scene understanding; train and validation annotations are released, while test annotations are withheld for evaluation.
